chain.label: AA had no guidance prohibiting load-closeout tasks during taxi
chain.trigger: lack of guidance prohibiting the performance of load closeout related tasks during taxi

chain.label: Captain began taxi before load closeout received
chain.trigger: he decided to begin the taxi before receiving the load closeout because the flight had a third flight crewmember

caused_by.evidence: a lack of guidance prohibiting the performance of load closeout related tasks during taxi increases the risk that a similar surface navigation error may occur

chain.label: 31L crossing clearance issued 4 minutes before taxiway K
chain.trigger: the ground controller instructed AAL106 to cross runway 31L at taxiway K

chain.label: Captain and FO absorbed in load-closeout/performance crosschecks during taxi
chain.trigger: she began performing required crosschecks of the load closeout information with takeoff performance information on her tablet

caused_by.evidence: load closeout-related tasks subsequently played a role in the captain's distraction and surface navigation error

chain.label: Captain omitted planned right turn onto taxiway K
chain.trigger: AAL106 crossed taxiway K and continued along taxiway B, which curved to the left

caused_by.evidence: salient cues to the airplane's position were present... but they were not sufficient to break through the distraction caused by the crew's load closeout-related tasks
because this clearance was issued 4 minutes before, visual indications were the primary cues of the airplane's position

chain.label: Ground controller distracted by other traffic and runway-change coordination
chain.trigger: the ground controller received a request from AAL107... established communications with an airport operations vehicle

chain.label: FO and FB, also absorbed in load-closeout tasks, failed to detect captain's missed turn
chain.trigger: the FO told investigators she was head-down dealing with tasks related to the load closeout

caused_by.evidence: the FO and FB were likely distracted from their primary duty of assisting the captain in safely taxiing the airplane by other operational activities, which resulted in the crew's loss of situational awareness

chain.label: RWSL activation logic illuminated REL too late
chain.trigger: the RELs illuminated as the airplane's nose was crossing the runway hold short markings, which was too late for the crew to perceive them and stop the airplane in a safe area

chain.label: Pre-crossing visual scan missed runway 4L signage and DAL1943
chain.trigger: the captain recalled looking left and right to clear the runway before entering it, and he did not see an airplane on the runway

caused_by.evidence: shortly thereafter, the airplane was directly facing taxiway J and the highly salient flashing yellow guard lights for runway 4L. A typical behavior pattern performed in that location involved taxiing onto taxiway J and crossing runway 4L

chain.label: AAL106 taxied across active runway 4L without ATC clearance
chain.trigger: the captain stated, 'clear left,' and the FO responded, 'clear right'... AAL106 continued across runway 4L

caused_by.evidence: the FO's nondetection of DAL1943 likely resulted from limitations of the human visual system for detecting small stationary targets in a complex visual scene in a limited time
the FO and FB were likely distracted... which resulted in the crew's loss of situational awareness
the ground controller... did not detect the flight crew's surface navigation error and subsequent turn onto taxiway J because he was performing a lesser priority task
the timing of the runway status light system, which activated too late to prevent the AAL106 crew from crossing the runway hold short line

chain.label: ASDE-X alert led to cancelled clearance and safe rejected takeoff
chain.trigger: the crew of DAL1943 rejected their takeoff, reaching a maximum groundspeed of about 105 knots, about 2,300 ft from the taxiway J intersection

caused_by.evidence: causing Delta Air Lines (DAL) flight 1943... to abort their takeoff roll on runway 4L
